v.en: O God, come to my assistance;

r.la: Et os meum annuntiábit laudem tuam.
r.en: And my mouth shall declare thy praise.

full.la: Prope est iam Dóminus, * Veníte, adorémus.
full.en: The Lord is now near * O come, let us adore Him.

short.en: O come, let us adore Him.

la: Veníte, exsultémus Dómino, iubilémus Deo, salutári nostro: præoccupémus fáciem eius in confessióne, et in psalmis iubilémus ei.
Quóniam Deus magnus Dóminus, et Rex magnus super omnes deos, quóniam non repéllet Dóminus plebem suam: quia in manu eius sunt omnes fines terræ, et altitúdines móntium ipse cónspicit.

Quóniam ipsíus est mare, et ipse fecit illud, et áridam fundavérunt manus eius veníte, adorémus, et procidámus ante Deum: plorémus coram Dómino, qui fecit nos, quia ipse est Dóminus, Deus noster; nos autem pópulus eius, et oves páscuæ eius.
Hódie, si vocem eius audiéritis, nolíte obduráre corda vestra, sicut in exacerbatióne secúndum diem tentatiónis in desérto: ubi tentavérunt me patres vestri, probavérunt et vidérunt ópera mea.
Quadragínta annis próximus fui generatióni huic, et dixi: Semper hi errant corde, ipsi vero non cognovérunt vias meas: quibus iurávi in ira mea: Si introíbunt in réquiem meam.
en: Come let us praise the Lord with joy: let us joyfully sing to God our saviour. Let us come before his presence with thanksgiving; and make a joyful noise to him with psalms.
For the Lord is a great God, and a great King above all gods. For the Lord will not cast off his people: for in his hand are all the ends of the earth, and the heights of the mountains are his.

For the sea is his, and he made it: and his hands formed the dry land. Come let us adore and fall down: and weep before the Lord that made us: For he is the Lord our God: and we are the people of his pasture and the sheep of his hand.

Today if you shall hear his voice, harden not your hearts: As in the provocation, according to the day of temptation in the wilderness: where your fathers tempted me, they proved me, and saw my works.
Forty years long was I offended with that generation, and I said: These always err in heart. And these men have not known my ways: so I swore in my wrath that they shall not enter into my rest.

v.la: Egrediétur Dóminus de loco sancto suo.
v.en: The Lord will come out of his place.

r.en: He comes to save his people.

text.la: Memor fuit in sǽculum * testaménti sui Dóminus Deus noster.
text.en: The memory of thy testament * will live forever, O Lord our God.

text.la: Auxit Dóminus * pópulum suum: et firmávit eum super inimícos eius.
text.en: The Lord increased his people exceedingly * and strengthened them over their enemies.

text.la: Edúxit Deus * pópulum suum in exsultatióne, et eléctos suos in lætítia.
text.en: The Lord brought forth * his people with joy, and his chosen with gladness.

text.la: Salvávit eos Dóminus * propter nomen suum.
text.en: The Lord saved them * for his own name's sake.

text.la: Oblíti sunt Deum * qui salvávit eos.
text.en: They forgot God * who saved them.

text.la: Cum tribularéntur * vidit Dóminus: et audívit oratiónem eórum.
text.en: And he saw when they were in tribulation * and he heard their prayer.

text.la: Clamavérunt ad Dóminum * et de necessitátibus eórum liberávit eos.
text.en: Then they cried to the Lord * and he delivered them out of their distresses.

text.la: Ipsi vidérunt * ópera Dei et mirabília eius.
text.en: These have seen * the works of the Lord, and his wonders.

text.la: Vidébunt recti * et lætabúntur, et intéllegent misericórdias Dómini.
text.en: The just see and rejoice * and understand the mercy of the Lord.

text.la: Pater Noster dicitur secreto usque ad Et ne nos indúcas in tentatiónem:
text.en: Our Father is said silently until And lead us not into temptation:.

text.la: A vínculis peccatórum nostrórum absólvat nos omnípotens et miséricors Dóminus.
text.en: May the Almighty and merciful Lord loose us from the bonds of our sins.

benedictio.la: Evangélica léctio sit nobis salus et protéctio.
benedictio.en: May the Gospel's holy lection Be our safety and protection.

source.en: Continuation of the Holy Gospel according to Luke

text.la: Anno quintodécimo impérii Tibérii Cǽsaris, procuránte Póntio Piláto Iudǽam. Et réliqua. Homilía sancti Gregórii Papæ Homilia 20 in Evangelia Redemptóris nostri Præcúrsor, quo témpore prædicatiónis offícium accéperit, memoráto Románæ reipúblicæ príncipe, et Iudǽæ régibus, designátur. Quia enim illum prædicáre veniébat, qui et ex Iudǽa quosdam, et multos ex géntibus redemptúrus erat: per regem géntium et príncipes Iudæórum prædicatiónis eius témpora designántur. Quia autem gentílitas colligénda erat, et Iudǽa pro culpa perfídiæ dispergénda, ipsa quoque descríptio terréni principátus osténdit: quóniam et in Romána república unus præfuísse descríbitur, et in Iudǽæ regno per quartam partem plúrimi principabántur.
text.en: In the fifteenth year of the reign of Tiberius Caesar, Pontius Pilate being governor of Judea. And so on. Homily by Pope St. Gregory the Great. 10th on the Gospels. The date, at which the Fore-runner of our Redeemer entered on his public office of preaching, is indicated to us by the name of the ruler of the Roman Commonwealth, and by those of the princes of Palestine. The time of his preaching is indicated by these names, because he came as the Fore-runner of Him Who was to be the Redeemer of some Jews and many Gentiles. Moreover in the enumeration of these worldly monarchs there is a foreshadowing of the fact, that the Gentiles were about to be gathered into one, and the Jews to be scattered abroad in punishment of their unbelief; in the whole heathen Commonwealth we find the title of one Emperor, but in the small kingdom of Judaea are mentioned four masters.

body.la: Egrediétur virga de radíce Iesse, et flos de radíce eius ascéndet:
body.en: There shall come forth a rod out of the stem of Jesse, and a flower shall grow out of his roots.

refrain.la: Et erit iustítia cíngulum lumbórum eius, et fides cinctórium renum eius.
refrain.en: And righteousness shall be the girdle of his loins, and faithfulness the girdle of his reins.

verse.la: Et requiéscet super eum spíritus Dómini: spíritus sapiéntiæ, et intelléctus: spíritus consílii, et fortitúdinis.
verse.en: And the Spirit of the Lord shall rest upon him the spirit of wisdom and understanding the spirit of counsel and might.

benedictio.en: God's most mighty strength alway be His people's staff and stay.

source.la: Voce étenim nostri Redemptóris dícitur: Omne regnum in seípsum divisum desolábitur. Liquet ergo, quod ad finem regni Iudǽa pervénerat, quæ tot régibus divísa subiacébat. Apte quoque non solum quibus régibus, sed étiam quibus sacerdótibus actum sit, demonstrátur: et quia illum Ioánnes Baptísta prædicáret, qui simul Rex et Sacérdos exsísteret, Lucas Evangelísta prædicatiónis eius témpora per regnum et sacerdótium designávit.
source.en: The blessed voice of the Saviour itself hath said, Every kingdom divided against itself is brought to desolation Luke xi. 17. And we may well look for the ruin of the Jewish state when we see it divided among so many rulers. We observe likewise that the names of the reigning priests as well as kings are given. The Evangelist Luke hath left on record the chiefs both of the monarchy and of the priesthood who held office when John the Baptist began to preach, because John preached Him Who is at once our Priest and our King.

body.la: Radix Iesse, qui exsúrget iudicáre gentes, in eum gentes sperábunt:
body.en: Behold, the root of Jesse that shall arise to bring forth judgment to the Gentiles, in him shall the Gentiles trust.

refrain.la: Et erit nomen eius benedíctum in sǽcula.
refrain.en: And his name shall be blessed for ever.

verse.la: Super ipsum continébunt reges os suum, ipsum gentes deprecabúntur.
verse.en: The Kings shall shut their mouths at him, to him shall the Gentiles seek.

benedictio.la: Ad societátem cívium supernórum perdúcat nos Rex Angelórum.
benedictio.en: May He that is the Angels' King to that high realm His people bring.

source.la: Et venit in omnem regiónem Iordánis, prǽdicans baptísmum pœniténtiæ in remissiónem peccatórum. Cunctis legéntibus liquet, quia Ioánnes non solum baptísmum pœniténtiæ prædicávit, verum étiam quibúsdam dedit: sed tamen baptísmum suum in remissiónem peccatórum dare non pótuit. Remíssio étenim peccatórum in solo nobis baptísmo Christi tribúitur. Notándum ítaque, quod dícitur: Prǽdicans baptísmum pœniténtiæ in remissiónem peccatórum: quóniam baptísmum, quod peccáta sólveret, quia dare non póterat, prædicábat: ut sicut incarnátum Verbum Patris præcurrébat verbo prædicatiónis, ita baptísmum pœniténtiæ, quo peccáta solvúntur, præcúrreret suo baptísmate, quo peccáta solvi non possunt.
source.en: And he came into all the country about Jordan, preaching the baptism of repentance for the remission of sins. It is evident from these words that John the Baptist not only preached, but also administered the baptism of repentance, and yet that baptism of repentance which he gave, was not really a baptism for the remission of sins. For there is only one baptism for the remission of sins, and that is our Christian baptism. It is worthy of note here that the words used are, preaching the baptism of repentance for the remission of sins, for he himself owned that his baptism was not the true baptism that washes away sin. Even as the Eternal Word of God made Flesh was greater than the preacher that went before Him, so was His holy baptism, by which our sins are washed away, far greater than that baptism of repentance which the Fore-runner preached, and which could never wash away sin.

body.la: Veni, Dómine, et noli tardáre: reláxa facínora plebi tuæ,
body.en: O Lord, come, and make no tarrying loosen the bonds of thy people.

refrain.la: Et révoca dispérsos in terram suam.
refrain.en: And gather together into their own land them that are scattered abroad.

verse.la: Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
verse.en: Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

text.la: Reliqua omittuntur, nisi Laudes separandæ sint.
text.en: Skip the rest, unless praying Lauds separately.

text.la: Deus, qui cónspicis, quia ex nostra pravitáte afflígimur: concéde propítius; ut ex tua visitatióne consolémur:
text.en: O God, Who seest that by reason of our sins we are sorely afflicted, mercifully grant unto us by thy visitation effectually to be comforted.
